chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who sees in sleep such that he feels desire, and he thinks that he has had a wet dream, but when he wakes up he does not see water on his garment nor on his body.
He عليه السلام said: "Ghusl is not obligatory upon him."
And he عليه السلام said: "'Ali عليه السلام used to say: Ghusl is only due from the greater water; so if he sees in his sleep but does not see the greater water, then no ghusl is obligatory upon him."

key_terms.غُسْلٌ: the obligatory ritual washing in this legal context
key_terms.ٱحْتَلَمَ: to have experienced a wet dream
key_terms.ٱلشَّهْوَةَ: sexual desire felt during the dream
key_terms.ٱلْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required in cases of janabah
key_terms.ٱلْمَاءَ: fluid or discharge referred to as the sign for obligation here
key_terms.ٱلْمَاءَ ٱلْأَكْبَرِ: the major discharge whose presence necessitates ghusl
key_terms.ٱلْمَنَامِ: sleep or dream-state in which the event is experienced

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl required if someone thinks he had a wet dream but finds no discharge after waking?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning janabah resulting from sleep. It states that merely experiencing desire or thinking one had a wet dream does not make ghusl obligatory unless the emission of fluid is actually found.
